title: What If You Had Nothing to Worry About
author: Summer Mulder
summary: Prompted by an Alan Watts clip heard while walking her dog, Mulder examines her own inability to imagine a version of herself without something to fix. The confession is specific: a spreadsheet to rebuild, a campaign to save, a fire to put out, a system to optimise. Worry, she notices, masquerades as responsibility and control while possibly being nothing more than noise, armour and a distraction from peace. Watts's framing of life as a divine theatrical play in which we have forgotten we are acting supplies her with an explanation for why every problem registers as the end of the world rather than another scene. She names the pattern entrepreneurship trained into her as a loop of emergency, where something is always broken and, if it is not, she assumes she missed something, because the absence of worry itself feels unsafe. Mulder pre-empts advice by noting she already meditates, journals and breathes, and that the problem is not knowing peace but trusting it. Her tentative conclusion is that real power lies in surrender rather than control, and that courage means sitting in the unknown rather than slaying dragons. She leaves the reader with the question she is still playing with: who would you be with nothing left to worry about.
points: Mulder's insight is that worry performs the feeling of responsibility without doing any of its work, which is why it is so hard to give up.
Naming the pattern a loop of emergency captures a specific occupational hazard: peace reads as inattention, so calm triggers a search for what has been missed.
She pre-empts the obvious advice by noting she already does the practices, relocating the problem from knowing what peace feels like to trusting it.
The Watts image of fear as heat from a flame, something that simply is rather than something to eliminate, underpins her shift from managing fear to not building an identity around it.
Her suggestion that the next system worth building is one teaching the body to exist without drama turns an optimiser's instinct against the habit itself.
quotes: Worry makes me feel like I’m doing something. Like I’m in control. Like I’m being responsible.
And we forgot we’re acting in it. We got so deep into our role, we started believing it was real.
And if it’s not? I assume I missed something. Because the absence of worry feels… unsafe.
Sometimes peace feels like neglect. Like I’m forgetting to check the locks or monitor the dashboard.
Maybe we’ve tied our identity to solving, saving, grinding and when nothing’s on fire, we panic. Because we don’t know how to just be.
I’m learning (not mastered) that real power isn’t in control. It’s in surrender.
What would you build if you weren’t building from fear? Who would you be if you had nothing left to worry about?
